subject: Pricing resilience swap & onboarding credit plan
messages:
From: Fran Lopez <fran@oliveretail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oliveretail.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing resilience swap & onboarding credit plan

Hi Jonas,

Renewal for our core inference contract is up at the end of October and we
need to get alignment on economics and onboarding support for the new
merchant AI rollout. Two asks from my side: first, a 12-month price hold
(or equivalent discount credit) to insulate us through holiday spikes; and
second, a short onboarding credit to cover the first 3 months of engineering
and adapter work (we estimate ~$60-90k).

We expect committed usage to increase from roughly 3M tokens/month to
~4.5M tokens/month over the next quarter. If there's a way to model a
stepped commit with an onboarding credit applied against initial invoices
(that's easiest for procurement), that would be ideal.

Can you put together a short proposal + mutual action plan by next week?
Procurement has a budget review on Oct 1 and legal prefers any term
changes captured in an addendum rather than a full replacement.

Attached: our last 3 months usage export (will send separately if you need
raw CSV).

Thanks,

Fran Lopez
Head of Platform, Oliver Retail
fran@oliveretail.com
+1 617-555-0184
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Fran Lopez <fran@oliveretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing resilience swap & onboarding credit plan

Hi Fran — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Happy to outline an
approach that should map to procurement and legal preferences. High level:

- Price resilience swap: 12-month price hold on current committed rate (we
  can convert to a dollar-denominated credit if you prefer) with a step-up
  true-up quarterly tied to the new commit band.
- Commit structure: bump from 3M to 4.5M tokens/month base commit;
  introduce a 3-tier stepped discount that increases as you cross each
  threshold (4.5M, 6M, 8M).
- Onboarding credit: one-time $75,000 credit applied evenly to the first
  three invoices after go-live (can appear as invoice line-item credit).
- Term: 12 months with quarterly true-ups and a PO + addendum (no full
  replacement needed).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll draft a short addendum and mutual action plan (attached MA plan)
   and share with procurement/legal.
2) Marissa, can you sanity-check the credit math and margin impact?
3) Kimberly, please prepare the SOW stub for onboarding work and the
   invoice schedule.
4) Fran, if this framework looks acceptable we can route to DocuSign and
   target signature by Sep 20 to make the Oct 1 budget cycle.

I attached a one-page MA plan and initial term sketch for your review.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0139

Attachments: draft_term_sketch_v1.pdf (term sketch), Oliver_Retail_MA-Plan.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OLIVER — margin check + SOW for onboarding credit

Jonas — quick internal note after looking at the numbers.

- $75k onboarding credit amortized across 3 invoices reduces realized
  ARR on month 1-3 by roughly $25k/mo; finance: what's the net margin impact
  vs our baseline? If legal wants credits on the invoice we'll need the
  GL mapping (Aditya, can you pick this up?).
- Commit math: if we move to a 4.5M base commit at discounted rates, our
  blended unit yield drops ~12% at current proposed bands. Approve only
  if we get a minimum 18-month payment cadence or upsell protection.
- SOW: Kimberly put together a stub SOW for integration work and an
  acceptance checklist (attached Renewal_Product_SOW.pdf). It limits the
  scope for the $75k (adapter + 2 weeks of on-call).

Requesting:
- Aditya: margin confirmation and GL mapping for credit posting.
- Karthik: any redline risk from the commit/band structure we should flag
  to legal (e.g., step-up triggers that create revenue recognition issues).
- Jonas: if we want to push the onboarding credit to $90k to secure the
  expansion, we should have a clear ask to present to the customer.

I'll hold on finalizing the SOW until we have finance sign-off.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: Renewal_Product_SOW.pdf, Oliver_Retail_MA-Plan.xlsx
From: Fran Lopez <fran@oliveretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@oliveretail.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing resilience swap & onboarding credit plan

Thanks Jonas (and team) — this looks like a good framework and aligns to
what procurement asked for. A few clarifications from our side:

- We prefer the credit to appear as an invoice-level credit rather than a
  discount so it's visible in our cost reporting.
- $75k works for the onboarding credit; if you can push to $85k we could
  commit to an accelerated 6-month cadence (rather than quarterly true-ups)
  and guarantee the 4.5M commit starting Nov 1.
- Legal: we'll take the addendum approach; procurement will issue a PO
  once we have the DocuSign link and final SOW.

Let's plan a quick 30-minute call tomorrow (Sep 16) to finalize language
and DocuSign routing. If you send the DocuSign link and the final SOW we
will aim to get the PO processed same day.

Regards,

Fran Lopez
Head of Platform, Oliver Retail
fran@oliveretail.com
+1 617-555-0184
